teaching.hint: If query times were considered in increasing order, could a discarded old request become relevant again?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Increasing query times move both fixed-duration boundaries forward. Per-server occurrence counts turn the active log range into a distinct server count.
solution_outline.approach: Sort logs by time and queries by time while preserving query indices. Admit logs through q, remove those strictly before q-x, and update per-server multiplicities and the number of positive counts. Return n minus this active count at each saved index.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: At each answered query the two pointers delimit exactly in-window logs, each server count is its multiplicity there, and the active count is the number of servers with positive multiplicity.
solution_outline.correctness: Sorted query boundaries never move backward, so every log enters and leaves at most once. The inclusive comparisons include both endpoint times. Updating the active count only at zero/nonzero transitions counts servers rather than requests. Every server is either active or has zero requests, making the complement exactly the requested answer; saved indices restore output order.
solution_outline.complexity: O(L log L + Q log Q + n) time including initialization, and O(n+Q) auxiliary space beyond the log sorting storage.
solution_outline.pitfall: Removing a server after just one of its requests expires is wrong while another request from it remains inside the window.

common_wrong_turns: Removing a server after just one of its requests expires is wrong while another request from it remains inside the window.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained both inclusive endpoints, all n servers including unlogged ones, unsorted input, and answer order.
